events.title: Proposed ruling: no_action (model confidence 0.78)
events.body:
The trip is a completed RydeX fixed-quote ride: the rider was billed 10.7 km / $24.93, which equals the quoted optimal distance, and billed distance did not exceed the optimal route [F4][F6]. Because RydeX is a non-metered service, the extra 4.5 km driven [F1] never entered the fare, so RD-2's metered branch (extra_km × distance_fare ÷ distance_km) yields nothing to refund; only an unpublished or unmet surcharge item could be refunded, and the bill contains only base, distance, time, platform fee, with waiting $0.00 and no toll item [F6][RD-2][FARE-1]. The refund portion of the claim therefore fails on the numbers, and the amount is nil.

The off-route segment 14:19–14:26 (5.03 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.39 km, +3.64 km, up to 1160 m off route) is nonetheless a real unexplained deviation, and RD-1 sets no percentage or kilometre threshold — any unexplained off-route stretch breaches the shortest-and-most-direct obligation [F1][F3][RD-1]. I checked each excuse. RD-4 does not apply: there is no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch and the speed-band records for AYER RAJAH EXPRESSWAY and CENTRAL EXPRESSWAY are only band 4 (30–39 km/h), i.e. not band 1 or 2, and a band record cannot exempt a segment on its own [F9][F10][F11][RD-4].

For RD-5, there is no rider consent at all: the in-app chat is empty, so nothing was sent by the rider before 14:19:10, and the driver's after-the-fact statement ("The GPS rerouted me, that's all") is a claim, not consent [F7][F8][RD-5]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment means the segment counts, so I find F3 "counts". RD-3 likewise gives no exemption — no rider-named place and no measured stop appears in the record [F7][RD-3].

That finding changes no money (fixed fare) but it does decide the account action: a non-exempt segment means the driver is in breach of RD-1, and the driver profile shows 2 upheld route disputes in the last 90 days, i.e. this is a repeated route breach, which calls for flagging the account for review [F14][RD-6]. The rider also asked for the detour to be "on record", which this ruling does.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the (empty) chat and the driver's statement — there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere, so the finding is "none" [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. Evidence is sufficient: the fare records, the GPS segment, the complete chat record and the traffic records settle every element this ruling needs [F3][F4][F6][F7][F11].

events.body:
RIDER: Your fare dispute is closed with no refund: your RydeX trip was a fixed quote, and you were billed 10.7 km and $24.93 — exactly the quoted amount. The longer route the driver took was never charged to you, so there is nothing to refund. We did record the detour in your complaint: the driver drove an unexplained off-route stretch during your trip, which breaks our shortest-route rule. Because this driver has repeated route issues recently, their account has been sent for review. Thanks for flagging it.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route on your completed RydeX trip. The fare is unchanged: it was a fixed quote, the rider was billed the quoted distance and amount, and no refund applies. However, the record shows an unexplained off-route stretch partway through the trip. The traffic conditions on those roads do not exempt it, and there was no rider agreement to the detour in the app chat. That makes it a breach of our shortest-and-most-direct route rule. As this is a repeated route issue on your account, your account has been sent to Ryde for review.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F3] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:19:10 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes no amount (fixed fare) but decides the RD-6 flag (the driver has a prior). Evidence — F8: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The GPS rerouted me, that's all. Nothing wrong with the fare.” (F8)

notices.text: Your fare dispute is closed with no refund: your RydeX trip was a fixed quote, and you were billed 10.7 km and $24.93 — exactly the quoted amount. The longer route the driver took was never charged to you, so there is nothing to refund. Because this driver has repeated route issues recently, their account has been sent for review. Thanks for flagging it.

We reviewed the route on your completed RydeX trip. The fare is unchanged: it was a fixed quote, the rider was billed the quoted distance and amount, and no refund applies. However, the record shows an unexplained off-route stretch partway through the trip. The traffic conditions on those roads do not exempt it, and there was no rider agreement to the detour in the app chat. That makes it a breach of our shortest-and-most-direct route rule. As this is a repeated route issue on your account, your account has been sent to Ryde for review.
